history.new: Closest prior work - J. Propp, 'How do you write one hundred in base 3/2?' (2017, endnote 3) proposes the family m -> p(x) with no results; Borodin et al., Minnesota J. Undergrad. Math. 6 (2021) (two-directional firing, always terminating); Bond-Levine 2016 (critical case, finite networks only). No statement of the uniform glider found (low-medium confidence).

limitations: Holds for all 28 surveyed rules (m <= 4, J <= 3, b_j <= 3); the general spreading step is unproved.
novelty_basis: Closest prior work - J. Propp, 'How do you write one hundred in base 3/2?' (2017, endnote 3) proposes the family m -> p(x) with no results; Borodin et al., Minnesota J. Undergrad. Math. 6 (2021) (two-directional firing, always terminating); Bond-Levine 2016 (critical case, finite networks only). No statement of the uniform glider found (low-medium confidence).
statement:
For every carry rule with sum_j b_j = m there is a unary start n whose sweep reaches a window dominating the
uniform-firing glider T = (T_1, ..., T_J), T_i = sum_{j >= i} b_j (or its g-sparse analogue, g the gcd of
the support of b); consequently its derivations from n are infinite. (Proved: T is a fixed point of the
window map and any window dominating T forces infinitely many firings.)
title: Carry rules with sum b = m never terminate from all unary starts (uniform glider)
